guide.description: A glob like *.txt lets you refer to a file by pattern instead of typing its exact name. The shell expands it against the current directory before the command ever sees it — if exactly one file matches, that's the file that gets read. Not every command expands globs here: head, tail, wc, grep, sed, awk, sort, uniq, and cut all do — cat and ls take their argument literally. Track 2 assumes you already know cd, ls, pwd, mkdir, mv, cp, rm, cat, and the pipes/text-tools from Track 1 — this track is about working faster.
